name: Shakshuka
summary: Eggs poached in a thick, smoky sauce of tomatoes, peppers, onion and cumin, cooked and served in one pan.
about: Shakshuka is eaten across North Africa, from Tunisia, Libya and Algeria to Morocco, and in Israel: eggs cooked in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce. It works as a weekend breakfast or a meat-free supper, and the only pan to wash is the one it is served in.
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan, about 30 cm across, with a lid, over medium heat. Add the onion and peppers and cook, stirring now and then, for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and sweet but not browned.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.

Stir in the tomato paste, chopped tomatoes, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough that a spoon drawn across the pan leaves a clear trail.
Make 8 hollows in the sauce with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each. Season the eggs with a pinch of salt.

Put the lid on and leave it over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites have turned opaque and firm and the yolks are still soft. Give it 3 to 4 minutes more for firm yolks, which most small children prefer.
Scatter over the coriander and parsley and serve from the pan.
prepNote: Make the sauce up to 2 days ahead and chill it; reheat until bubbling before adding the eggs.
